newsitem.title: USA: Arafat, Netanyahu invited to U.S. meetings.
newsitem.headline: Arafat, Netanyahu invited to U.S. meetings.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will make separate visits to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton in the coming weeks, the White House said on Wednesday.
The announcement was made a day after Netanyahu and Arafat reached a long-sought agreement on an Israeli troop withdrawal from the West Bank city of Hebron.
"We do expect to see Chairman Arafat and Prime Minister Netanyahu here sometime fairly early during the course of the year, separately," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

A senior administration official said there were "no plans for a summit" between the Middle Eastern leaders. He suggested Jordan's King Hussein and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak might also make separate visits to Washington.
"We anticipate that there will be meetings sometime in the first quarter with at least the two major figures, and often others are coming in this same time frame," the official said.
In telephone conversations Tuesday night with Netanayahu and Arafat, Clinton said that "he hoped to see them here soon so they'd have a chance to discuss the next step," the official said.

McCurry said the United States would now focus its attention on "building trust and confidence" between the parties as they implement the new agreement and move on to deal with remaining peace roadblocks.
